_about: Hand-kept register of work that only people can do. tools/readiness.py counts the entries; nothing here is a typed total. Add an entry when the event really happened, with its date and where the notes are. An empty list means it has not happened.

accessibility_journeys.label: Keyboard only: start, finish the first lesson, answer an exercise (WCAG 2.2: 2.1.1, 2.4.7)
Screen reader: lesson text, board squares and exercise feedback are announced in order
Narrow screen (320 px wide): nothing overlaps, no sideways scrolling (1.4.10)
accessibility_journeys.notes: [V] by script in the browser preview at 320x640: no sideways scroll on 16 routes (home, curriculum, map, practice, lesson, analysis, library, settings, roadmap, openings, play, placement, lab, games, plan, electives). Overlap was not judged by eye; not a real-device test.

accessibility_journeys.label: Text enlarged to 200 percent: lesson, exercise and menus still usable (1.4.4)
accessibility_journeys.notes: [V] by script at 200% root font size, 320 px wide: no sideways scroll on home, curriculum, practice, a lesson, library (settings pending); fixed Analysis and lesson overflow first. Menus and exercise answering not driven by hand; the browser zoom path is separate.

accessibility_journeys.label: Reduced motion setting respected on the map and the board
accessibility_journeys.notes: Read from the code, not run with the setting on: index.css has a blanket prefers-reduced-motion rule (animation and transition near zero) plus specific rules for board pieces, map glow, side drawer, cover info and up-next marks; PathView, appearance.ts and useAnimatedNumber read the same media query. Still untested with the real operating-system setting, so it stays unticked.
